# glinet Provider

Manages GL.iNet routers that run v4 firmware. The provider is tested on a GL-AXT1800 with firmware 4.7.0 and 4.8.3. Other models and firmware versions can have different API methods.

~> **Warning:** some resources can cut the access to the router: [`glinet_wan`](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/ryanrishi/glinet/latest/docs/resources/wan), [`glinet_lan`](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/ryanrishi/glinet/latest/docs/resources/lan) and [`glinet_wifi_interface`](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/ryanrishi/glinet/latest/docs/resources/wifi_interface). Read the warnings on their pages before you apply them.

Destroy of a resource disables a feature that exposes the router or acts on its own (`glinet_firewall_dmz`, `glinet_ddns`, `glinet_tailscale`, `glinet_zerotier`, `glinet_reboot_schedule`), removes a list item (`glinet_lan_static_lease`, `glinet_client_block`, `glinet_firewall_port_forward`, `glinet_firewall_rule`, `glinet_wireguard_client_group`, `glinet_wireguard_client_config`, `glinet_wireguard_server_peer`), and leaves a plain setting unchanged on the router (the other resources).

## Example Usage

```terraform
terraform {
  required_providers {
    glinet = {
      source = "ryanrishi/glinet"
    }
  }
}

# The arguments can also come from GLINET_HOST, GLINET_USERNAME and GLINET_PASSWORD.
# With all three set, the block can be empty: provider "glinet" {}
provider "glinet" {
  host     = "http://192.168.8.1"
  username = "root"
  password = var.glinet_password
}

variable "glinet_password" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `host` (String) URL of the router, with the scheme, for example `http://192.168.8.1`. When it is not set, the provider uses the `GLINET_HOST` environment variable. Defaults to `http://192.168.8.1`.
- `password` (String, Sensitive) Password for the login to the router, the same as for the web UI. When it is not set, the provider uses the `GLINET_PASSWORD` environment variable. One of the two is required.
- `username` (String) User name for the login to the router. When it is not set, the provider uses the `GLINET_USERNAME` environment variable. Defaults to `root`.
